headlines.text: Looking back to 2026, when Darby Allin vs. Kevin Knight fought tooth and nail for the AEW World Heavyweight Title, appearing on Dynamite, rated 8.19 ? a hard-hitting, high-quality battle. Fresh off saving Kevin Knight from an MJF beatdown the week before, Allin turned away his third different World Title challenger in as many weeks in another hard-fought battle.

On this day in 2020, Matt Hardy skipped the warm-up and went straight to headlining on debut in a Falls Count Anywhere match, appearing on Dynamite, rated 8.34 ? a genuinely great match. Matt Hardy's AEW in-ring debut, spiraling into a wild, roaming brawl through the stadium ? Hardy switched personas mid-match, got locked in an ice machine, and fought through an ATM and a golf cart chase, a chaotic preview of the Stadium Stampede war to come.

2022 brought us this moment: Konosuke Takeshita didn't ease in ? their first AEW match was the main event against Jay Lethal, appearing on Rampage, rated 7.28 ? a well-paced, entertaining battle. Takeshita's official AEW television debut, stepping in against Jay Lethal on short notice ? a strong first showing that made clear the Japanese star had real staying power in AEW, even in a losing effort.

secondaries.text: On a Wednesday in 2026, back when Gunns & Ace wasted no time making an impression, debuting right in the main event as a team, appearing on Collision, rated 7.04 ? a solid showing.
On this day in 2026, it was a welcome sight as Bryan Keith returned to the ring after 3 months away, appearing on Dynamite.
On this day in 2022, Yuka Sakazaki made their long-awaited return to AEW television after just under 10 months away, appearing on Rampage.
